Only the binary arm is feasible (hky_last_fall_degree for m=2; ic corpus + msolve -v 2 for m=3, l<=4). (2) 'Residual 0 or 1 in all cells' has no null: if reg(Sym^m E) is n-independent (the cited claim) and d_F is flat over n=7..13 (the brief says small n shows no growth, d_F<=k+2 / fits ceil(l/2)+4), the residual is flat too and the 'true' prediction passes under the max-model, a constant-offset model, and plain additivity alike. The 'false' prediction (residual grows with n) needs n beyond reach. (3) 'reg(subspace-only system)' is undefined; 'max F4 degree' is a strategy-dependent proxy, not last fall degree or Hilbert regularity, and regularity of a homogeneous cover ideal is not the same invariant as the affine descent degree with field equations. (4) The arXiv 2610.16350 premise is unverified, so the Sym^m(E) arm has no reference value to calibrate against. (5) Scaling: even a clean additivity pass at toy n only moves the open lever-1 question into the subspace-only term; it proves no bound unless the subspace term is shown to be bounded, so it is an accounting device, not evidence about n=131. Runtime: binary m=2 (n=7..13, l=3..5) well under 1 CPU-minute; m=3 l<=4 (12 vars) msolve under a few minutes; fits the 18-minute budget once the F_1031 arm is dropped.
